<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Form of Stock Option and Restricted Stock Unit Agreements.</I> For stock option
and restricted stock unit awards granted in May 2010 and thereafter, the Compensation Committee approved the inclusion of a &#147;claw-back&#148; provision in AMD&#146;s form of stock option agreement and form of restricted stock unit agreement for
senior vice presidents and above, which includes all of the Named Executive Officers. This claw-back provision provides that in the event AMD is required to prepare an accounting restatement due to AMD&#146;s material noncompliance with any
financial reporting requirement under the securities laws, the Compensation Committee will review all equity-based compensation awarded to any employee at the senior vice president level and above. If the Compensation Committee (in its sole
discretion) determines that any such employee was directly involved with fraud, misconduct, and/or gross negligence that contributed to or resulted in such accounting restatement, the Compensation Committee may, to the extent permitted by governing
law and as appropriate under the circumstances, recover for the benefit of AMD all or a portion of the equity-based compensation awarded to such employee, including, without limitation, by cancelation, forfeiture, repayment, and/or disgorgement of
profits realized from the sale of AMD&#146;s securities; provided,</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">33 </FONT></P>

compensation awarded more than 18 months prior to the date of the first public issuance or filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (whichever first occurs) of the financial document embodying such financial reporting
requirement.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:3.00em; text-indent:-1.00em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;<I>Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct.</I> AMD&#146;s Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct
provide that, among other things, in the event AMD is required to prepare an accounting restatement due to AMD&#146;s material noncompliance with any financial reporting laws, AMD may pursue all remedies to recover any incentive-based or other
compensation (including equity awards) paid or granted to its employees or agents to the extent required by and permitted under applicable law.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">AMD continues to monitor the rule-making actions of the SEC and NYSE with respect to the development, implementation, and disclosure of claw-back
provisions/policies. AMD will revise its claw-back provisions/policies in the future as required by applicable law.</FONT></P></TD></TR>
<TR>
<TD HEIGHT="16"></TD>
<TD HEIGHT="16" COLSPAN="4"></TD></TR>
<TR>
<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Align pay practices with sound risk management</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" COLSPAN="3"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee endeavors to structure AMD&#146;s executive compensation program to motivate and reward the
Named Executive Officers for appropriately balancing opportunity and risk, such as investment in key initiatives designed to accelerate AMD&#146;s growth in existing and new markets, while at the same time avoiding pay practices that incentivize
excessive risk-taking.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee believes that
AMD&#146;s executive compensation program fosters AMD&#146;s objectives and strategies while maintaining appropriate risk mitigators, such as:</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Multiple internal controls and approval processes intended to prevent manipulation
of outcomes;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Pay mix that represents an appropriate balance of base&nbsp;pay versus variable pay
and short-term versus long-term incentives;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Caps on performance-based compensation opportunities;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Incentive programs that incorporate company-wide financial goals (e.g., non-GAAP
operating income) that are quantitative and measurable;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Claw-back policies/provisions; and</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock ownership
guidelines.</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Named Executive Officers are subject to stock ownership guidelines</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" COLSPAN="3"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In October 2011, the Compensation Committee increased the ownership levels under AMD&#146;s stock ownership guidelines to strengthen the alignment of the interests of
our executive officers and stockholders and to increase visibility of our executive officers&#146; stock ownership. All executive officers are subject to the revised stock ownership guidelines, including the Named Executive Officers. Set forth below
are the current minimum stock ownership requirements for our executive officers:</FONT></TD></TR>

<TD HEIGHT="8"></TD>

STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Chief Executive Officer:</FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The lesser of (i) the number of shares equivalent to three times the then-current annual base salary divided by the average of the closing stock prices of AMD&#146;s common stock
for the 30-day period up to and including the Officer Achievement Date (as defined below) or (ii) the number of shares equivalent to three times the then-current annual base salary divided by the average of the closing stock prices of AMD&#146;s
common stock for the 30-day period immediately preceding and ending on the date that the President and/or the CEO was appointed, rounded to the nearest 5,000 shares.</FONT></TD></TR>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>AMD&#146;S EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION FRAMEWORK </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>AMD&#146;s Executive Compensation Philosophy and Objectives </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our executive compensation philosophy is to provide
compensation and benefit programs that enable us to attract, retain, and motivate high caliber executive officers, to motivate these executive officers to achieve our short-term and long-term objectives and strategies, and to support career
development and succession goals. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">To implement
this philosophy, the Compensation Committee has established the following objectives: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Link rewards to achievement of AMD&#146;s objectives and strategies to drive the creation of sustainable stockholder value;
</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Provide the opportunity to reward superior individual and Company performance; </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Manage pay structure and programs globally, while recognizing local market practices and conditions; </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Mitigate incentives for executive officers to undertake excessive risks by, among other things, balancing fixed and variable pay;
</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Provide an appropriate return on investment on the overall program spending; and </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Encourage equity ownership to align the interests of our executive officers and stockholders. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Role of the Compensation Committee </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee regularly reviews the alignment
of our executive compensation program with the strategies and needs of our business, market trends, changes in competitive practices, individual performance, Company performance, and the interests of our stockholders. Based on this review, the
Compensation Committee approves the compensation of the Named Executive Officers, including, without limitation, base salary, short-term incentive awards (which are in the form of a cash performance bonus), long-term equity awards, and other
benefits. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Role of Management </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee believes that even the best
advice of a compensation consultant or other outside advisors must be combined with the input from senior management and the Compensation Committee&#146;s own individual experiences and judgment to arrive at the proper alignment of compensation
philosophy, objectives, and programs. In 2011, the Chief Executive Officer, interim Chief Executive Officer, Chief Talent Officer and General Counsel and Corporate Secretary worked closely with the Compensation Committee. These individuals worked
with the Compensation Committee in formulating the specific plan and award designs, performance measures, and performance levels (i.e., threshold, target, and maximum) necessary to align AMD&#146;s executive compensation program with its objectives
and strategies. Mr.&nbsp;Seifert served as interim Chief Executive Officer of AMD from January 2011 to August 2011, and in such role, Mr.&nbsp;Seifert worked closely with the Compensation Committee. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Generally, the Chief Executive Officer reviews with the
Compensation Committee his performance evaluations of each of the other Named Executive Officers and his recommendations (except with respect to his own compensation) regarding base salary adjustments, short-term incentive awards, and long-term
equity awards for the other Named Executive Officers to ensure alignment with the Compensation Committee&#146;s pay-for-performance design principle. However, all final decisions regarding the compensation of the Named Executive Officers are made by
the Compensation Committee. The Board and Compensation Committee conduct their own performance assessment of the Chief Executive Officer and no management recommendation is made with regard to his compensation. In light of the transition in the
composition of AMD&#146;s senior leadership team in 2011, Mr.&nbsp;Seifert, as acting Chief Executive Officer, also conducted performance evaluations of the Named Executive Officers. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">36 </FONT></P>



<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">While certain members of management attended the Compensation Committee&#146;s meetings in
2011 upon invitation, they did not attend either private sessions or portions of any other meetings of the Compensation Committee where executive compensation determinations were made by the Compensation Committee. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Assessment of Individual Performance </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Named Executive Officers&#146; compensation is impacted
by individual performance. At least annually, the Board of Directors evaluates the performance of the Chief Executive Officer. For the purpose of setting compensation, the Compensation Committee annually assesses the performance of the Chief
Executive Officer based upon the Board of Director&#146;s evaluation. Additionally, the Compensation Committee annually assesses the performance of the other Named Executive Officers based upon the Chief Executive Officer&#146;s report and
evaluation of such officers&#146; individual performance. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The assessment of the Named Executive Officers&#146; individual performance is an objective and subjective assessment of accomplishment and contribution to AMD. For a further description of the individual
performance factors that impacted the Named Executive Officers&#146; compensation in 2011, see the section titled &#147;2011 Executive Compensation Decisions&#148; below. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Role of the Compensation Consultant </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During 2011, the Compensation Committee retained Compensia,
Inc., as its compensation consultant to obtain objective, expert advice on executive and director compensation. Compensia advised the Compensation Committee on a variety of compensation-related issues in 2011, including: </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>

</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition to the above, Compensia assisted the Compensation Committee in performing a comprehensive reassessment of the methodology used
in evaluating AMD&#146;s executive compensation, as further described in the section titled &#147;&#151;Competitive Pay Analysis&#148; below. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2011, Compensia did not provide any services to AMD, or receive any payments from AMD, other than in its capacity as a consultant to
the Compensation Committee. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the course of
conducting its activities, Compensia attended meetings of the Compensation Committee and presented its findings and recommendations for discussion. During 2011, Compensia also met with senior management to obtain and validate data and review
materials. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Competitive Pay Analysis
</I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation
Committee generally aims to set each Named Executive Officer&#146;s total direct compensation (i.e., base salary, target cash performance bonus, and target long-term equity awards) between the 50</FONT><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> and 75</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP
STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> percentile of the competitive market data. However, the purpose of the competitive pay analysis is not to supplant
retention and continuity considerations within the senior leadership team of AMD, among other things, when the Compensation Committee approves executive compensation. Accordingly, each Named Executive Officer&#146;s total direct compensation may
vary from the 50</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> and 75</FONT><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> percentile of the competitive market data due to one or more factors
that the Compensation Committee deems fundamental to the best interests of the Company and its stockholders. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">37 </FONT></P>



<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Each year, the Compensation Committee evaluates how our pay practices and the Named
Executive Officers&#146; compensation levels compare to the competitive market for executive talent. Each year the Compensation Committee generally reviews a custom group of peer companies, in combination with industry-specific survey data, to
develop a reasonable representation of the &#147;competitive market&#148; with respect to AMD&#146;s executive pay levels and pay policies and practices. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Reassessment of the Methodology Used to Perform the Competitive Pay Analysis </I></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In 2011, the Compensation Committee, with the assistance of
Compensia, performed a comprehensive reassessment of the methodology used in analyzing AMD&#146;s executive compensation. Specifically, the Compensation Committee made significant changes to AMD&#146;s custom peer group, survey sources, and market
position matches as follows: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">38 </FONT></P>



<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The composition of the Custom Peer Group changed in 2011 with the addition of seven new
companies (i.e., CA; CommScope; Juniper Networks; Marvell Technology; NetApp; Symantec; and Western Digital) and the removal of two companies (Intel Corp. and LSI). The 2011 peer companies were primarily selected based upon their (i)&nbsp;industry,
(ii)&nbsp;revenues (roughly .05x to 2.5x AMD&#146;s revenues) and (iii)&nbsp;market capitalization. The Compensation Committee believes that the composition of the 2011 Custom Peer Group better reflects industry-comparable companies of AMD.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In general, the Compensation
Committee used the Custom Peer Group as its primary source in analyzing the competitiveness of Named Executive Officers&#146; compensation, and used the Industry-Specific Survey Data to supplement the Custom Peer Group to develop a &#147;market
consensus&#148; of the competitive market data. The comprehensive reassessment of the methodology used in our executive compensation analysis resulted in a decrease in the compensation reference points at the 50</FONT><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> and 75</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP
STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> percentiles for the incumbent Named Executive Officers, in comparison to 2010. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In light of the transition in the
composition of AMD&#146;s senior leadership team in 2011, the Compensation Committee determined that it was in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders to encourage retention and continuity within AMD&#146;s existing senior leadership
team rather than ensure the total direct compensation of Messrs. Seifert, Ghilardi, Wolin and Bergman fell within the
50</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> and 75</FONT><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th</SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"> percentile of the competitive market data. Notwithstanding this
objective, all of the Compensation Committee&#146;s decisions in 2011 were taken, as in the past, within the framework of the Compensation Committee&#146;s overall objective of linking a significant percentage of our executives&#146; compensation to

<TR>
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Short-Term Incentives</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">(in the
form of a cash</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">performance bonus)</FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" COLSPAN="9"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Generally, short-term incentives, in the form of a cash performance bonus, are provided to the Named Executive Officers
under the EIP and are intended to focus the Named Executive Officers on AMD&#146;s short-term objectives. The short-term incentive goals and related target levels are approved at the Compensation Committee meeting shortly after the commencement of
the applicable performance period, the intent of which is to comply with Section&nbsp;162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code regarding performance-based compensation.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For 2011, only Messrs Seifert, Ghilardi, Papermaster, Wolin and Bergman
participated in the EIP. Mr. Meyer resigned from AMD in January 2011 and, therefore, was not eligible to participate in the EIP for 2011. Pursuant to the terms of his employment agreement, Mr. Read&#146;s participation in the EIP commences in
2012.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For 2011, the Compensation Committee approved short-term
incentive award opportunities under the EIP, based upon our achievement of predetermined &#147;non-GAAP operating income&#148; goals over two six-month performance periods (i.e., December&nbsp;26, 2010 to July&nbsp;2,&nbsp;2011 and July&nbsp;3, 2011
to December&nbsp;31, 2011). While the amount of the 2011 short-term incentive award was measured and calculated based upon AMD&#146;s performance over two six-month performance periods, the participating Named Executive Officers&#146; award, if
earned, was paid in a single payment after the end of the year.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For 2011, the Compensation Committee selected non-GAAP operating income as the performance measure for the short-term incentive award to incentivize the
participating Named Executive Officers to focus on improving AMD&#146;s profitability, a key objective for 2011. The Compensation Committee views non-GAAP operating income as a multi-dimensional measure that encourages the Named Executive Officers
to focus on maximizing revenue while, at the same time, controlling expenses.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For purposes of the EIP, &#147;Non-GAAP operating income&#148; was calculated as AMD&#146;s operating income (calculated in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
(&#147;GAAP&#148;)) excluding the impact of (i) amortization expense incurred in 2011 relating to intangible assets we acquired in the ATI Technologies, Inc. acquisition, (ii) a charge related to a payment made to GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. in the first
quarter of 2011, (iii) a charge related to a legal settlement in the first quarter of 2011, and (iv) restructuring charges.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee and senior management both believe that AMD&#146;s non-GAAP operating income better reflects AMD&#146;s profitability than GAAP
operating income because it excludes items that are not indicative of AMD&#146;s core operating performance. Specifically, the adjustments are intended to:</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Align the short-term incentive award with the underlying performance of AMD&#146;s
core business;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-1.50em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Avoid volatile, artificial inflation or deflation of the short-term incentive award
due to either unusual items in the performance period or items that are not indicative of AMD&#146;s core operating performance; and</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">40 </FONT></P>

<TD VALIGN="bottom"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-2.00em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">(1)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;If AMD&#146;s performance falls between the threshold, target,
and maximum achievement levels, the Bonus Opportunity is linearly interpolated to determine the actual bonus payment.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-2.00em"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">(2)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with Mr. Ghilardi leaving the Company in February 2012, he was no longer eligible to receive a cash performance bonus for 2011.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-2.00em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">(3)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Papermaster&#146;s target cash performance bonus was prorated based upon the time
he served as Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer of AMD in 2011.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-2.00em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">(4)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Papermaster was appointed Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer of
AMD effective on October&nbsp;24, 2011, and, therefore, Mr. Papermaster was not eligible to earn a cash performance bonus for the first six-month performance period in 2011. As our non-GAAP operating income fell below the threshold level for the
second six-month performance period, he did not earn a cash performance bonus for 2011. Additionally, Mr. Papermaster&#146;s target Bonus Opportunity of 100% for the second half of 2011, as compared to the other participating Named Executive
Officers&#146; of 150%, was aligned with the competitive market data.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:2.00em; text-indent:-2.00em"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1">(5)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.
Bergman was not eligible to receive a cash performance bonus for 2011 due to his resignation from AMD on September&nbsp;27, 2011.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee designed the short-term incentive awards to reward superior performance by providing for progressively increasing payments as
our performance exceeded the target level, and correspondingly providing for no payment unless a threshold level of performance was achieved. The Compensation Committee reviews and certifies our achievement of the performance goals before any
payments are made. This review and certification is generally performed at the first regularly scheduled Compensation Committee meeting following the end of the year with any payout of the short-term incentive award occurring shortly thereafter.
Under the terms of the EIP, the Compensation Committee has the authority to reduce any participating Named Executive Officer&#146;s short-term incentive award prior to payment. For 2011, the Compensation Committee did not exercise this authority in
connection with any of the participating Named Executive Officers.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For further information about the participating Named Executive Officers&#146; cash performance bonus under the EIP for 2011, see the &#147;2011 Summary
Compensation Table&#148; below.</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<TD VALIGN="bottom" ALIGN="center"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><B>Basis of Design</B></FONT></P><HR WIDTH="90" SIZE="1" NOSHADE STYLE="color:#000000"></TD></TR>


<TR>
<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Special Performance Bonus</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with Mr. Seifert&#146;s service as interim Chief Executive Officer of AMD from January 10, 2011 to August 24, 2011, he
was eligible to receive a special performance bonus. The amount of the special performance bonus was in the Compensation Committee&#146;s sole discretion; provided that it could not exceed $100,000 per month in which Mr. Seifert served as interim
Chief Executive Officer.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In recognition of Mr. Seifert&#146;s
contributions as interim Chief Executive Officer, he received a special performance bonus of $746,000, paid in lump-sum. The Compensation Committee believes the special performance bonus was reasonable and appropriate to recognize Mr. Seifert&#146;s
critically important interim leadership and specific achievements in (i) his leadership during the first half of 2011 in which AMD was able to achieve its first and second quarter earnings guidance for 2011, (ii) his efforts in accelerating
AMD&#146;s growth in China, (iii) his implementation of plans for efficient, repeatable, and scalable systems for key operational processes, (iv) his successful handling of staff performance issues, and (v) working productively with the Board of
Directors. Except for this performance bonus, Mr. Seifert did not receive any other compensation for his service as interim Chief Executive Officer of AMD.</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P></TD></TR>
<TR>
<TD VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Long-Term Incentives</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">(in the
form of stock options and RSUs)</FONT></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For 2011, the Compensation Committee granted the Named Executive Officers (other than Mr. Meyer) equity awards under our long-term
incentive program. These awards were granted under our 2004 Plan.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Messrs. Seifert, Ghilardi, Papermaster, Wolin and Bergman each received time-based stock options and time-based RSUs. Mr. Read, under the terms of his
employment agreement, received time-based stock options, performance-based stock options, time-based RSUs and performance-based RSUs.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The time-based stock options are intended to align the Named Executive Officers&#146; interests with our stockholders&#146; interests, because there is no
financial gain to a Named Executive Officer unless our stock price appreciates. In general, time-based stock options are granted with an exercise price equal to 100% of the fair market value of our common stock on the grant date, vest over a three
year period, and expire seven years after the grant date.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The
time-based RSU awards are intended to encourage executive retention, manage share dilution, recognize individual performance, and align the Named Executive Officers&#146; interests with our stockholders&#146; interests, because the value of the
award is tied to the market value of our common stock. In general, time-based RSUs vest in three equal annual installments commencing approximately one year from the grant date, except for Mr. Read&#146;s sign-on RSU award that vests 100% on the
one-year anniversary of his hire date.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For 2011, the Compensation
Committee generally believed that an equivalent value of time-based stock options and time-based RSUs offered the Named Executive Officers a competitive level of equity-based compensation, while balancing the retention value of RSUs with the
performance aspect of stock options.</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In an effort to increase the
competitiveness of Mr. Read&#146;s new-hire compensation package, while at the same time reinforcing the link of his new-hire equity awards to the creation of stockholder value, Mr. Read was also granted a performance-based stock option and
performance-based RSU award. The performance-based stock option has an exercise price equal to 100% of the fair market value of our common stock on the grant date and vests in three equal annual installments commencing on the first anniversary of
the grant date if (i) the market-base component is satisfied meaning that the weighted average closing price of our common stock over any 30-day period during the three-year vesting period is equal to or greater than $11.00 per share and (ii) Mr.
Read continues his employment with AMD through the applicable vesting date. Similarly, the performance-based RSU award vests in three equal annual installments commencing on the first anniversary of the grant date if (i) the market-base component is
satisfied meaning that the weighted average closing price of our common stock over any 30-day period during the three-year vesting period is equal to or greater than $11.00 per share and (ii) Mr. Read continues his employment with AMD through the
applicable vesting date (collectively, the &#147;Performance-Award Vesting Requirements&#148;).</FONT></P></TD></TR>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>OTHER ASPECTS OF AMD&#146;S EXECUTIVE
COMPENSATION PROGRAM </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Management
Continuity Agreements, Change in Control Agreements, or Change in Control Arrangements </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We have entered into a management continuity agreement, change in control agreement or other change in control arrangement with each of the Named Executive Officers. These arrangements are designed to
encourage the Named Executive Officers&#146; continued services in the event of a potential change in control of AMD and to allow for a smooth leadership transition upon a change in control of AMD. In addition, these arrangements are intended to
provide incentives to the Named Executive Officers to execute the wishes of our Board of Directors, even in the event that the Board of Directors takes an action that may result in the elimination of a Named Executive Officer&#146;s position with
AMD. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">45 </FONT></P>



<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under the terms of these arrangements, a Named Executive Officer is entitled to certain
compensatory payments and benefits only if (i)&nbsp;a &#147;change in control&#148; of AMD occurs and (ii)&nbsp;the Named Executive Officer&#146;s employment is terminated, or the Named Executive Officer is constructively discharged, within two
years of the change in control of AMD. The Compensation Committee believes this structure strikes a balance between incentives and executive hiring and retention without providing payments and benefits to the Named Executive Officers who continue to
enjoy employment with an acquiring company in the event of a change in control of AMD. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In April 2009, AMD adopted a policy to, in general, not enter into any new management continuity agreements or change in control agreements containing an excise tax gross-up provision. In accordance with
emerging best practices, in February 2011, AMD adopted a policy clarifying that it will not enter into any new change in control arrangements containing an excise tax gross-up provision. Messrs. Read&#146;s, Seifert&#146;s, and Papermaster&#146;s
change in control agreements do not provide for excise tax gross-ups and Mr.&nbsp;Wolin entered into his management continuity agreement prior to April 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In March 2010, AMD adopted a policy to not enter into any change in control arrangements with any executive officer that provide him or
her with a cash severance payment (upon both a change in control of AMD and a subsequent termination of employment) in excess of (i)&nbsp;two times the sum of the respective executive officer&#146;s base salary and target cash bonus, plus
(ii)&nbsp;a prorated cash bonus for the year in which termination occurs assuming performance at target level. Mr.&nbsp;Read&#146;s change in control arrangement and Messrs. Seifert&#146;s and Papermaster&#146;s change in control agreements comply
with this limitation. Mr.&nbsp;Wolin entered into his management continuity agreement prior to the adoption of this policy. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For a detailed description of the payments and benefits payable under these arrangements, see the section titled &#147;Executive
Compensation&#151;Change in Control Arrangements&#148; below. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Severance Arrangements </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with Mr.&nbsp;Meyer&#146;s resignation in January 2011, Mr.&nbsp;Meyer and AMD entered into a Separation Agreement and Release. The terms of Mr.&nbsp;Meyer&#146;s severance payments and
benefits under the Separation Agreement and Release were fully consistent with his employment agreement and are described in the section titled &#147;Executive Compensation&#151;Employment and Related Agreements&#148; below. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Additionally, under the terms of Mr.&nbsp;Read&#146;s
employment agreement and Mr.&nbsp;Ghilardi&#146;s offer letter, they are entitled to certain severance payments and benefits as further described in the section titled &#147;Executive Compensation&#151;Employment and Related Agreements&#148; below.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Except for Messrs. Meyer, Read and Ghilardi and
as discussed in the section titled &#147;&#151;Management Continuity Agreements, Change in Control Agreements, or Change in Control Arrangements&#148; above, AMD is not under any contractual obligation to provide severance payments and benefits to
any of the Named Executive Officers. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Deductibility of Executive Compensation </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Section&nbsp;162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code limits the deductibility of nonperformance-based compensation paid to the Chief Executive
Officer and any of the three other most highly compensated executive officers of AMD, other than the Chief Financial Officer, to $1&nbsp;million in any tax year. In establishing total compensation for such executives, the Compensation Committee
considers the effect of Section&nbsp;162(m). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our
objectives and strategies may not always be consistent with the requirements of Section&nbsp;162(m) for full deductibility. Therefore, deductibility under Section&nbsp;162(m) is just one consideration and not the determinative factor in setting our
executives&#146; compensation, and certain compensation paid by AMD in the future may not be fully deductible under Section&nbsp;162(m). </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">46 </FONT></P>

filings, nor will it be deemed to be soliciting material or deemed filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>COMPENSATIO<A NAME="tx306562_12"></A>N COMMITTEE REPORT
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee of the Board has
reviewed and discussed with management the Compensation Discussion and Analysis included in this proxy statement. Based on this review and discussion, the Compensation Committee recommended to the Board that the Compensation Discussion and Analysis
be included in AMD&#146;s proxy statement for our 2012 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:54%; text-indent:-2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">COMPENSATION COMMITTEE </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:54%; text-indent:-2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">March&nbsp;6, 2012 </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:54%; text-indent:-2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">H. Paulett Eberhart, Chair </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:54%; text-indent:-2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">John E. Caldwell </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:54%; text-indent:-2%"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Craig A. Conway </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:54%; text-indent:-2%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Nicholas M. Donofrio </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">47 </FONT></P>

<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>COMPENSATION PO<A NAME="tx306562_13"></A>LICIES AND PRACTICES </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Compensation Committee reviewed our compensation policies
and practices for employees generally and concluded that these policies and practices do not create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on AMD. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In reaching this conclusion, the Compensation Committee, with
the assistance of management, assessed the Company&#146;s executive and broad-based compensation programs to determine if any of them created undesired or excessive risks of a material nature. The assessment included (i)&nbsp;a review of the
Company&#146;s compensation policies and practices for employees generally, (ii)&nbsp;identification of the risks that could result from such policies and practices, (iii)&nbsp;identification of the risk mitigators and controls, and
(iv)&nbsp;analysis of the potential risks against the risk mitigators and controls and AMD&#146;s business strategy and objectives. Although the Compensation Committee reviewed all of AMD&#146;s compensation programs, the Compensation Committee
focused on the programs that have variability of payout and in which employees could directly affect the payout of incentives. These programs included AMD&#146;s 2011 EIP, 2005 Annual Incentive Plan, Sales Incentive Plan and 2004 Plan. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In performing the assessment and reaching its conclusion, the
Compensation Committee noted the following factors that reduce the likelihood of undesired or excessive risk-taking: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our overall compensation levels are competitive with the market. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our compensation practices and policies appropriately balance base pay versus variable pay and short-term versus long-term incentives.
</FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Although AMD&#146;s 2011 EIP, 2005 Annual Incentive Plan and Sales Incentive Plan have variability of payout, any potential risks associated with such
plans are controlled or mitigated by: (i)&nbsp;the performance goals being multi-dimensional, thereby increasing the range of performance over which incentives are paid; (ii)&nbsp;the performance goals being aligned with AMD&#146;s business
strategies and objectives and/or being company-wide financial goals that are quantitative and measurable; (iii)&nbsp;the use of sliding payout scales, with the payouts linearly interpolated for performance falling between threshold, target and
maximum achievement levels; (iv)&nbsp;the ability of the Compensation Committee and/or management to exercise discretion to reduce payouts, including in connection with extraordinary or unanticipated company events; (v)&nbsp;the existence of
multiple internal controls and approval processes that are intended to prevent manipulation of performance; and (vi)&nbsp;the incentive opportunities being capped. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT
SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Although the grant of equity awards under AMD&#146;s 2004 Plan could incentivize employees to, among other things, focus on increasing AMD&#146;s
short-term stock price rather than the creation of sustainable stockholder value, that risk is controlled by: (i)&nbsp;awarding a combination of stock options and RSUs; (ii)&nbsp;the vesting provisions being aligned with stockholders&#146;
interests; and (iii)&nbsp;AMD&#146;s stock ownership guidelines for our executive officers. In addition, AMD prohibits its employees, including the Named Executive Officers that remain employed with AMD, from engaging in certain hedging transactions
in its common stock. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We have implemented claw-back provisions and policies, as described in more detail above. </FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We maintain the DIA which allows eligible employees, including the Named Executive Officers, to voluntarily defer receipt of a portion of
their salary, bonus and any commission payments until the date or dates selected by the participant. Participants may defer up to 50% of annual base salary and/or 100% of commissions and bonuses. Earnings on the deferred accounts are based on the
performance of the investment funds selected by the participants. Participants make a deferral election prior to the year in which the compensation is earned that may not be terminated or changed during the year for which it was made. Generally, we
make a contribution to the participant&#146;s account if his/her annual base salary minus Section&nbsp;401(k) contribution before the deferral is greater than the compensation limit for 401(k) plans. The contribution, if any, is equal to the lesser
of (i)&nbsp;50% of the deferred compensation credited to the participant&#146;s account for the year and (ii)&nbsp;a discretionary percentage of the participant&#146;s base salary in excess of the eligible 401(k) compensation limit for the year
minus the participant&#146;s 401(k) contributions. For 2011, AMD&#146;s discretionary contribution percentage under option (ii)&nbsp;above was 4.5%. For 2011, Messrs. Wolin and Meyer did not elect to contribute to the DIA; therefore, pursuant to the
terms of the DIA, we did not make any contributions to their accounts for 2011. We did not make any contributions to Mr.&nbsp;Bergman&#146;s account for 2011 because pursuant to the terms of the DIA participants must be employed with AMD as of the
end of the fiscal year to receive a matching contribution, and Mr.&nbsp;Bergman resigned as an employee in September 2011. Participants are 100% vested in the value of their accounts. Participants may select their desired benchmark investment
fund(s) in which their accounts are deemed to be invested and may change their investment elections at any time, with such change effective from the next business day. The amount of investment gain or loss that is credited to the participant&#146;s
account depends on the participant&#146;s investment election. Currently, we are utilizing the investment funds, except the Lifestyle Funds, available under variable life insurance policies insured by John Hancock Life as the benchmark investment
funds. For Messrs. Wolin, Bergman and Meyer, the investment return was calculated by taking the aggregate </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">51 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">
gain or loss in 2011 and dividing it by aggregate balance as of the beginning of 2011. Because Mr.&nbsp;Ghilardi began participating in the DIA during 2011and did not have a balance in his
account at the beginning of 2011, we calculated his investment return by using the dollar weighted rate of return, also known as the internal rate of return. For 2011, the investment return credited to the DIA accounts of Messrs. Ghilardi, Wolin,
Bergman and Meyer were -13.7%, -3.1%, -5.0% and 1.1%, respectively, based on their investment elections for their DIA accounts. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The DIA accounts are distributed following a participant&#146;s termination of employment with us unless the participant has elected an
in-service withdrawal (scheduled or hardship withdrawal). At the time a participant makes his/her deferral election, he/she may elect a different form of distribution for such year&#146;s deferred compensation. The participant may elect a single
lump sum distribution or annual installment distributions over three to ten years. The default form of distribution is a single lump sum. A participant may change the form of distribution election, subject to the terms of the DIA. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A participant may elect to withdraw all or part of his/her
account while employed by us, subject to the terms of the DIA. The in-service withdrawal date must be at least two years after the plan year in which the election was made. An in-service withdrawal date may be changed, subject to the terms under the
DIA. An unscheduled payment may also be made, subject to the terms of the DIA. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%;padding-bottom:0px;"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Mr.&nbsp;Meyer&#146;s Separation Agreement and Release.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</I>On January&nbsp;10, 2011,
Mr.&nbsp;Meyer resigned as President and Chief Executive Officer and director of AMD, effective January&nbsp;10, 2011 (the &#147;Separation Date&#148;). Mr.&nbsp;Meyer executed a Separation Agreement and Release upon his departure, which summarized
the payments and benefits he received under his employment agreement upon an Involuntary Termination Without Cause. Specifically, on or about the first business day following the six-month anniversary of the Separation Date, we paid Mr.&nbsp;Meyer
an aggregate amount equal to $8,565,818 (which includes $15,818 of interest earned on his separation payment of $8,550,000 calculated based on the then applicable short-term Applicable Federal Rate for federal tax purposes). For a period of
18&nbsp;months following the Separation Date, we are paying for Mr.&nbsp;Meyer&#146;s COBRA premium payments for himself and his eligible dependents under the Company&#146;s group medical and dental plans and for the full cost of his life insurance
coverage comparable to the life insurance coverage provided to Mr.&nbsp;Meyer while he was our President and Chief Executive Officer. In 2011, we also paid as additional tax withholding remitted to the appropriate taxing authority $41,543,
representing the amount calculated to pay income and employment taxes due as a result of our payment of these health and welfare benefits, and we will pay as additional tax withholding remitted to the appropriate taxing authority an amount
calculated to pay any income and employment taxes due as a result of providing such benefits in 2012. On the Separation Date, all equity awards then held by Mr.&nbsp;Meyer subject to vesting and based on Mr.&nbsp;Meyer&#146;s continued service with
us (i.e., non-performance vesting awards) accelerated and became fully vested. In addition, the exercise period for any stock option awards was extended to the earlier of the fifth (5</FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="1"><SUP
STYLE="vertical-align:baseline; position:relative; bottom:.8ex">th </SUP></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">)&nbsp;anniversary of the date of termination or the expiration of such awards. Pursuant to the Separation Agreement
and Release, Mr.&nbsp;Meyer affirmed his continuing obligations under his Proprietary Information and Invention Assignment Agreement dated November&nbsp;13, 1995. He is also subject to a two-year non-compete covenant and a two-year non-solicitation
covenant as described above. The payments and benefits set forth in Mr.&nbsp;Meyer&#146;s Separation Agreement and Release are consistent with his employment agreement. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We entered into either a management continuity agreement,
change in control agreement or other change in control arrangements with each of the Named Executive Officers. These arrangements are designed to encourage the Named Executive Officers&#146; continued services in the event of a potential change in
control of AMD and to allow for a smooth transition upon a change in control of AMD. In addition, these arrangements are intended to provide incentives to the Named Executive Officers to execute the wishes of our Board of Directors, even in the
event that the Board of Directors takes an action that may result in the elimination of a Named Executive Officer&#146;s position with AMD. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under the terms of these arrangements, a Named Executive Officer is entitled to certain compensatory benefits only if (i)&nbsp;a
&#147;change in control&#148; of AMD occurs and (ii)&nbsp;the Named Executive Officer&#146;s employment is terminated, or the Named Executive Officer is constructively discharged, within two years of the change in control of AMD. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In April 2009, we adopted a policy to, in general, not enter into new management continuity agreements or change in control agreements
with excise tax gross-up provisions. In accordance with emerging best practices, in February 2011, we adopted a policy clarifying that we will not enter into any new change in control arrangements with excise tax gross-up provisions.
Mr.&nbsp;Read&#146;s change in control arrangements and Messrs. Ghilardi&#146;s, Papermaster&#146;s, and Seifert&#146;s change in control agreements do not provide for excise tax gross-up provisions; Mr.&nbsp;Wolin entered into his agreement in

March 2010, we adopted a policy to not enter into any change in control arrangements with executive officers that provide AMD&#146;s executive officers&#146; cash severance payments (upon both a change in control of AMD and a subsequent termination
of employment) in excess of (i)&nbsp;two times the sum of the respective officer&#146;s base salary and target cash bonus, plus (ii)&nbsp;a prorated cash bonus for the year in which termination occurs assuming performance at target level.

under our equity incentive plans become fully vested (i)&nbsp;if the successor refuses to assume or substitute similar awards for outstanding awards, upon the change in control, as defined in the plans or (ii)&nbsp;if the successor assumes or
substitutes similar awards for outstanding awards and the participant&#146;s employment is terminated by us for any reason (other than for misconduct) or by the participant due to a constructive termination within one year following a change in
control, upon such termination of employment. </FONT></P>

</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>CERTAIN RELATI<A NAME="tx306562_22"></A>ONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our Audit and Finance Committee monitors and reviews issues
involving potential conflicts of interest and related party transactions. In doing so, the Audit and Finance Committee applies our Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct, which provides that directors, Named Executive Officers and all other
employees are expected to avoid any relationship, influence or activity that would cause or even appear to cause a conflict of interest. Our Principles of Corporate Governance require a director to promptly disclose to the Chairman of the Board any
conflict of interest involving the director. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>The GLOBALFOUNDRIES Manufacturing Joint Venture Transaction.</I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On October&nbsp;6, 2008, we entered into
a Master Transaction Agreement with ATIC and WCH, acting through its general partner, West Coast Hitech G.P., Ltd. which was further amended on December&nbsp;5, 2008. The transaction was completed on March&nbsp;2, 2009. Pursuant to the Master
Transaction Agreement, we and ATIC formed GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (&#147;GF&#148;), who manufactures semiconductor products and provides certain foundry services to us. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement, we contributed
certain manufacturing&#150;related assets and liabilities to GF in exchange for securities of GF and the assumption of specified AMD liabilities by GF.&nbsp;ATIC contributed approximately $1.4 billion of cash to GF in exchange for GF equity
securities and convertible notes, and ATIC paid $700 million in cash to us in exchange for a portion of our GF equity securities. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, at the completion of the transaction, we issued to WCH 58&nbsp;million shares of our common stock and warrants to purchase
35&nbsp;million shares of our common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $125 million. The warrants are currently exercisable and have a ten-year term. Also, pursuant to the Master
Transaction Agreement, for so long as WCH and its permitted transferees beneficially own at least 10% of our outstanding common stock, WCH has the right to designate one person for election to our Board of Directors. On March&nbsp;2, 2009, WCH
designated and our Board appointed Waleed Muhairi to the Board. Mr.&nbsp;Muhairi continued to serve on our Board in 2010 and 2011 and is a director nominee for the Annual Meeting. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At the completion of the transaction, we also entered into a
Shareholders&#146; Agreement, a Funding Agreement and a Wafer Supply Agreement with ATIC and GF. The Shareholders&#146; Agreement and Funding Agreement were amended and restated as of December&nbsp;27, 2010. The Shareholders&#146; Agreement was
terminated as of March&nbsp;4, 2012, and AMD was removed as a party from the Funding Agreement as of March&nbsp;4, 2012. The Wafer Supply Agreement was amended as of April&nbsp;2, 2011 and as of March&nbsp;4, 2012. Certain terms of these agreements
are summarized below. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Both WCH and ATIC are
either directly or indirectly wholly-owned subsidiaries of Mubadala Development Company PJSC, a joint stock company incorporated in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and which is owned by the Government of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Mr.&nbsp;Muhairi is the
Chief Operating Officer of Mubadala and is the Chairman of ATIC. As of March&nbsp;2, 2009, ATIC owned 60 percent of GF on a fully converted basis and as of March&nbsp;5, 2012, ATIC owned 100 percent of GF on a fully converted basis. As of
March&nbsp;5, 2012, WCH beneficially owned approximately 19.34 percent of AMD&#146;s outstanding common stock. </FONT></P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">66 </FONT></P>
